nss.whoWeAre.label: Profile
nss.whoWeAre.subtitle: Born from a vision of selfless service, we transform ordinary students into extraordinary nation-builders.
nss.whoWeAre.para1: National Service Scheme (NSS) — India's largest voluntary youth organization. Launched on 24th September, 1969 — the birth centenary of Mahatma Gandhi — we were created with one powerful purpose: to develop the personality of students through community service.
nss.whoWeAre.para2: Under the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, Government of India, we operate across thousands of colleges and universities, empowering young minds to serve the nation while building leadership, discipline, and empathy.
nss.whoWeAre.para3: Our motto — "Not Me But You" — captures the essence of democratic living: the welfare of others before self. This is not just a slogan for us; it is a way of life.
nss.whoWeAre.fact3Value: Youth Affairs & Sports, Govt. of India
nss.whoWeAre.fact4Value: 8 spokes of the Konark Wheel — 24 hours of selfless service
nss.whatWeDo.label: Our Mission
nss.whatWeDo.heading: This is What
nss.whatWeDo.subtitle: We don't just talk about change — we create it. Here's how we serve our community, our nation, and our future.
nss.whatWeDo.card1Desc: Blood donation drives, health awareness programmes, village adoption, and door-to-door welfare campaigns that touch lives directly.
nss.whatWeDo.card2Desc: Tree plantation drives, cleanliness campaigns, waste management initiatives, and building an eco-conscious generation.
nss.whatWeDo.card3Desc: Teaching underprivileged children, digital literacy workshops, and awareness campaigns that break the cycle of ignorance.
nss.whatWeDo.card4Desc: Emergency response during floods, earthquakes, and pandemics — NSS volunteers are always among the first to arrive.
nss.whatWeDo.card5Desc: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, sanitation drives, health camps, and spreading awareness about preventive healthcare.
nss.whatWeDo.card6Desc: Cultural exchange programmes, unity rallies, and campaigns against discrimination — building one India, together.
nss.giveGet.label: The Exchange
nss.giveGet.heading: What Happens When
nss.giveGet.headingAccent: You Join As a NSS Volunteer
nss.giveGet.subtitle: It's a two-way journey. You invest in us, and we invest in your transformation. Here's what the exchange looks like.
nss.giveGet.give1: Your time, energy, and compassion — the most powerful gifts you own.
nss.giveGet.give2: Minimum 120 hours of community service spread across 2 years.
nss.giveGet.give3: Active participation in camps, rallies, cleanliness drives, and social programmes.
nss.giveGet.give4: Your unique skills — whether it's teaching, organizing, creating, or leading.
nss.giveGet.get1: UGC-recognized certificate and grace marks on your academic record.
nss.giveGet.get2: Leadership, teamwork, communication, and real-world problem-solving skills.
nss.giveGet.get3: A powerful network of like-minded changemakers and lifelong friends.
nss.giveGet.get4: Priority weightage in government jobs, competitive exams, and higher education.
nss.giveGet.get5: Memories, experiences, and a sense of purpose that transforms your entire life.
nss.bbCollege.label: Our College
nss.bbCollege.heading: Life at Banwarilal Bhalotia
nss.bbCollege.subtitle: This is where the action happens. Here's what makes our NSS unit at BB College, Asansol, truly special.
nss.bbCollege.card1Desc: Every year, we organize an annual 7-day residential special camp where volunteers live, learn, and serve together in adopted villages. It's the highlight of our NSS calendar — a life-changing experience of community living and service.
nss.bbCollege.card2Desc: From NSS Day (24th September) to Republic Day, Gandhi Jayanti to International Yoga Day, World Environment Day to National Youth Day — we celebrate every occasion that inspires service and patriotism.
nss.bbCollege.card3Desc: Regular blood donation camps organized on campus, saving hundreds of lives in Asansol and surrounding areas. Our volunteers lead by example — rolling up their sleeves for those in need.
nss.bbCollege.card4Desc: Cleanliness drives across campus and surrounding communities, keeping Mahatma Gandhi's vision of a clean India alive. Every broom we pick up is a step towards a better tomorrow.
nss.bbCollege.card5Desc: Taking to the streets to spread awareness on critical issues — health, environment, gender equality, substance abuse, and social harmony. Our voice reaches where textbooks cannot.
nss.bbCollege.card6Desc: Reaching underprivileged communities with education, healthcare essentials, and emotional support. We believe service is not charity — it is our responsibility as future citizens.
nss.history.label: Our History
nss.history.heading: Why NSS
nss.history.subtitle: We were born from a simple belief — that the youth of this nation can build the India of tomorrow, one act of service at a time.
nss.history.desc1: NSS was launched by the Government of India on 24th September, 1969 — the birth centenary of Mahatma Gandhi. It started with 37 universities covering 40,000 students.
nss.history.desc2: To develop student personality through community service, bridge the gap between educated youth and rural communities, and instil a sense of social responsibility.
nss.history.desc3: From 37 universities in 1969 to over 40,000+ NSS units across India today. Over 40 lakh student volunteers actively serve the nation every single year.
nss.history.desc4: NSS continues to be India's most powerful platform for youth empowerment. Every camp, every drive, every act of service adds to a legacy that began with one simple belief.
nss.cta.heading: Your Journey of Service
nss.cta.subtitle: Join our NSS family at Banwarilal Bhalotia College and be the change you want to see. Every great transformation begins with a single step — take yours today.

nss.spotlight.title: Krishan Kumar Gupta
nss.spotlight.subtitle: The First NSS Volunteer of India
nss.spotlight.desc: Formally recognized as India's very first NSS volunteer, Mr. K.K. Gupta enrolled during the historic first orientation camp at Rajghat, Kirori Mal College (University of Delhi) in June 1969. For decades, he has remained an active guide and a source of inspiration for millions of young volunteers across the nation.
